name: Ard
overview: Ard is a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, identified as a grandson or son of Benjamin through Bela. He is listed among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, marking him as part of the foundational genealogy of Israel during the patriarchal period. His mention is brief but situates him within the early history of the Israelite people.
namesAndTitles: The name Ard means 'hunchbacked' in Hebrew, a proper name recorded in Genesis 46:21. Additionally, a similar name, Addar, meaning 'glorious,' appears in 1 Chronicles 8:3, though it is not explicitly linked to the same individual. Neither name is indicated as being divinely given.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Ard as a son of Bela, who is a son of Benjamin, establishing Ard as a direct descendant within the Benjaminite lineage. These relationships are explicitly stated in Genesis 46:21 and Numbers 26:40. No further family details are provided beyond this lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Ard's significance lies primarily in his inclusion in the genealogical record of the tribe of Benjamin, highlighting the continuity of God's covenant people as they moved into Egypt. His presence in the list of those who went to Egypt underscores the fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham regarding his descendants. Though not prominent in narrative events, Ard represents the faithful lineage through which Israel's history unfolded.
